data.title: Bitwise operations
data.statement:
Perform a bitwise operation between two binary numbers, and return the result as a decimal number.

A bitwise operation applies a logical operation to each pair of corresponding bits in two binary numbers.

Built-in bitwise operators available in your language may be used. Alternatively, you may implement the operations using the definitions below.

Assume [[x]] and [[y]] are bits. The required operators are:
- [[x]] {{AND}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = [[y]] = 1; otherwise 0.
- [[x]] {{OR}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = 1 or [[y]] = 1; otherwise 0.
- [[x]] {{XOR}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] ≠ [[y]]; otherwise 0.
- [[x]] {{NAND}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = 0 or [[y]] = 0; otherwise 0.
- [[x]] {{NOR}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = [[y]] = 0; otherwise 0.
- [[x]] {{XNOR}} [[y]] = 1 if [[x]] = [[y]]; otherwise 0.
data.constraints:
Possible values of [[op]]: {{AND}}, {{OR}}, {{XOR}}, {{NAND}}, {{NOR}}, {{XNOR}}.
1 ≤ [[a]] < 2^25
1 ≤ [[b]] < 2^25
[[a]] and [[b]] always have the same number of digits.
Either [[a]] or [[b]] can have leading zeros so that lengths match.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Perform a bitwise operation between two binary numbers, and return the result as a decimal number.

A bitwise operation applies a logical operation to each pair of corresponding bits in two binary numbers.

Built-in bitwise operators available in your language may be used. Alternatively, you may implement the operations using the definitions below.

Assume x and y are bits. The required operators are:
- x AND y = 1 if x = y = 1; otherwise 0.
- x OR y = 1 if x = 1 or y = 1; otherwise 0.
- x XOR y = 1 if x ≠ y; otherwise 0.
- x NAND y = 1 if x = 0 or y = 0; otherwise 0.
- x NOR y = 1 if x = y = 0; otherwise 0.
- x XNOR y = 1 if x = y; otherwise 0.
Input
op a b: A bitwise operator, followed by two binary numbers, separated by a space.
Output
A decimal number, result of the bitwise operation.
Constraints
Possible values of op: AND, OR, XOR, NAND, NOR, XNOR.
1 ≤ a < 2^25
1 ≤ b < 2^25
a and b always have the same number of digits.
Either a or b can have leading zeros so that lengths match.
Example
Input
AND 1010 1001
Output
8
